subject.title: [Bug]: Embedded runner "Network connection lost" when LLM generates a tool call with large parameters (param generation latency > underlying request timeout)

question: For OpenRouter-routed Anthropic models that stay silent while generating large tool-call arguments, should OpenClaw change default timeout behavior, add provider-specific streaming/argument handling, or keep the current default and rely on explicit provider timeout configuration?
rationale: The source supports the failure shape, but the durable fix trades off stall detection latency, existing provider defaults, compatibility with OpenRouter's OpenAI-compatible route, and provider-specific streaming support.

options.title: Live repro plus provider-specific fix
options.body: Require a live OpenRouter Anthropic repro, then implement the narrowest provider/runtime change that makes large tool arguments stream or otherwise avoid the silent-window failure.

options.title: Document timeout mitigation only
options.body: Keep the current watchdog default and document `models.providers.openrouter.timeoutSeconds` as the supported workaround for slow large-argument generations.

options.title: Raise or relax cloud idle timeout
options.body: Increase the default cloud idle window or retry behavior globally, accepting slower detection of genuine stalled provider streams.

recommendation.title: Live repro plus provider-specific fix
recommendation.body: Require a live OpenRouter Anthropic repro, then implement the narrowest provider/runtime change that makes large tool arguments stream or otherwise avoid the silent-window failure.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant recent history points to steipete for embedded-runner timeout and provider-runtime policy decisions.
